Summary: A manual save and reload brings most of the warehouse loot back while stash bags stored in your vehicle stay put, so one site can be emptied over and over.
Steps or trigger: 1. Drive Jason's personal vehicle to the red Apollo Aggregates warehouse east of Hamlet in South Vice-Dale County, north of Key Lento. 2. Loot the cocaine on the back office table and in the office safe, the cash stash bag by the van inside, and the cocaine in the teddy-bear vans inside and in the yard. 3. When a stash bag is full, store it in your vehicle and go back for the rest. 4. Make a manual save, then load it. You respawn at Jason's house and the bags are still in the vehicle. 5. Return to the warehouse. Most loot is back. Repeat until the vehicle is full. 6. Sell at Brian's Lockup in southwest Key Lento (keypad code 7700) or at Donnie's Trailer in Key Lento while they are open (Chapter 1). Compare both quotes on the map first. From Chapter 2 the goods fence is Dunk in Port Gellhorn. 7. Wait for the fence's text, then collect the cash from the mailbox at Jason's safehouse and deposit it at an ATM.
Payout: Beebom: about $11,280 on the first run and $8,640 on each later run. Game Rant: about $8,000 every five minutes. GTA BOOM: one full clear was quoted $14,400 by Donnie and $12,720 by Brian. Nerpah: $13,000 per run; the "$250k per hour" in the video title is not backed up in the video.
Tips: Use manual saves, never autosaves. If loot does not return, reload again or wait a few in-game days. If you run it in Chapter 1, spend the proceeds on gear and move $5,000 into Family Savings before starting the mission Tourist Trap. That money cannot be withdrawn later. Unverified shortcut to try at your own risk: three November 20 videos say you can skip the save and instead drive away until the site unloads, then drive back. If the loot is not back, fall back to the manual save and reload.
Caveats: Still reported working on November 20, 2026 by Beebom (now titled "Tested and Working"), Stealthy Gaming and IGN, though DamnModz says players report mixed results. Guides disagree on when to use it. Stealthy Gaming and Pro-Gamer.gg say to wait for Chapter 2 because Chapter 1 money is wiped. IGN and PowerPyx say Brian's Lockup closes when Chapter 1 ends, and Tech4Gamers says Donnie stops buying after the mission Swamped, so in Chapter 2 the bags have to go to Dunk in Port Gellhorn (after the mission Slam Dunk), who pays low rates. No guide found so far shows a Chapter 2 run with a payout, so every figure here is a Chapter 1 figure. In Chapter 1, pocket cash, the BuckMe checking balance and the floor stash are all lost when Tourist Trap starts. Only money moved into Family Savings carries into Chapter 2, and it can never be withdrawn, so it raises your checking limit rather than your spending money. The first savings goal is $5,000. The first checking limit is $15,000 and payments above it are held as pending. Pocket cash is capped at $20,000 and lost when Wasted or Busted. GTA BOOM found three loot sources that do not come back, and notes the site is an Illegal Operation that restocks by design, so this may be a fast cooldown rather than a true duplication. games.gg and the CodeKingGTA repo still list no independently verified, version-stamped money glitch. A no-save variant is claimed in three November 20 videos but not verified. JoeyRahmz says driving the van parked out front away for 15 to 20 seconds and back brings the loot back, and that this van holds 10 stash bags. Bubs agrees the van holds 10 but says to leave it parked as the stash and drive a second vehicle away for 20 to 25 seconds, and claims about $43,000 in about 10 minutes from 12 bags, a figure the video does not demonstrate. AZAP says to drive your own car away until the barn unloads, and warns against using vehicles parked at the site, so the three disagree on the vehicle. AZAP credits JoeyRahmz for gameplay clips, so those two are not independent. None states a build or shows the fence payment arriving, and no written guide repeats the claim. Bubs labels it "after the patch", but no post-launch patch has been released. Kotaku quotes a player who says about $10,000 in bagged stash money and a collectible card were gone after a save and reload. The post does not say whether the bags were in a vehicle.
Reported by: Beebom, Game Rant, GTA BOOM, Nerpah, Stealthy Gaming, IGN

Summary: A built-in cheat that adds $250,000 each time it is entered. It only unlocks after the main story is finished.
Steps or trigger: 1. Finish the main story to unlock the cheat. 2. Open the phone with D-pad Up, hold L1 (LB on Xbox) and press R1 (RB). 3. Enter Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right.
Payout: $250,000 per entry, repeatable in the same session.
Tips: Keep a separate manual save from before you enter any cheat.
Caveats: Rock Paper Shotgun and PC Gamer both say you cannot save after entering a cheat, so the money does not carry into your saved game. Rock Paper Shotgun adds that trophies and achievements are off for that session. PC Gamer says each cheat also needs its own challenge completed after the story, and lists the money cheat challenge as unknown. It is a sandbox tool, not a way to bank money.
Reported by: Rock Paper Shotgun, PC Gamer, Leonida Interactive

Glitch: Store robbery timer reset via mission restart
Money potential: About $200 per store (one guide claims $1,500+ per loop)
Summary: Restarting and then quitting a mission that opens with a cutscene clears the closed timers on robbed stores, so the same stores can be robbed again straight away. IGN describes the method and several creators show it.
Steps or trigger: 1. Rob store registers in one area until the stores close and grey out on the map. 2. Lose the police, then go to a story mission marker that opens with a cutscene. "Meet Brian" is the one most videos use. 3. When the cutscene starts, pause and choose Restart Mission. 4. When the cutscene starts again, pause, choose Quit Mission and confirm. Creators say quitting without restarting first is not reliable. 5. Check the map. The robbed stores should be open again and you keep the cash. Repeat the route.
Payout: Timesaver.GG puts store stick-ups at up to about $200 each, so the loop is slow per store. Pro-Gamer.gg claims $1,500 to $15,000 or more per loop for a Key Lento route, which no other outlet backs up. Video titles claiming "$100K in minutes" or "5 million per hour" give no per-store figures.
Tips: Deposit cash at an ATM between loops. One narrator lost all his money when his vehicle was impounded. Pro-Gamer.gg suggests the burger joint and gas station near Jason's house in Key Lento and skipping Ammu-Nation.
Caveats: IGN, Vice City DB and Polygon all expect Rockstar to patch this. DamnModz says players report mixed results. Creators do not agree on how it works: most say it resets the store timers, while one video describes it as rolling back to an earlier save while the money carries over. No write-up states the console or build tested, and the first video used Xbox button prompts. If you use it in Chapter 1, the Chapter 1 cash wipe at Tourist Trap applies. games.gg still lists no version-verified money glitch.
Reported by: IGN, Vice City DB, MillGaming, Toughest Glitches, Pro-Gamer.gg

Glitch: Pay 'n' Spray daily sale limit reset
Summary: Pay 'n' Spray only buys a few stolen cars per in-game day. Resting or reloading is reported to reset the count so you can keep selling.
Steps or trigger: 1. Scan cars with the WAiNK app and steal the most valuable ones you can. 2. Sell at any Pay 'n' Spray until it stops buying (about three or four cars). 3. Rest or reload the game to roll the day over, then sell again.
Payout: Forbes: early cars pay hundreds to over $1,000 each, with a limit of roughly three to four sales a day. Leonida Intel cites PC Gamer for a limit of three.
Tips: Repair the car first. Fences pay less for damaged vehicles.
Caveats: This looks like intended day-cycle behavior rather than a bug. Guides disagree on when Pay 'n' Spray starts buying stolen cars: Forbes describes it as early game, while PowerPyx and Leonida Intel place it in Chapter 3.

Summary: No working car duplication method has been published for GTA VI. Claims exist, but none shows steps, two copies of the car, a sale and a save that keeps the money.
Payout: Nothing demonstrated. For scale, the most valuable car documented so far, the Pegassi Infernus '96, sells for $17,160 according to GTABase.
Tips: When a method appears, look for an uncut clip showing the balance before and after, a save and reload, and the build number.
Caveats: Rechecked on November 20, 2026: both CodeKingGTA repos still list vehicle duplication as "Unverified for GTA VI", and the duplication guides that turn up in searches are for GTA Online in GTA V. GTA Online duplication relied on online garages and sessions, and GTA VI has no online mode. Stolen street cars are not kept unless registered, and registered cars are sold from the Stored Vehicles tab at Pay 'n' Spray, which is where any future duplicate would have to be cashed in.
Reported by: Community rumor; r/speedrun item 13 notes money glitch claims of unknown validity

Caveats: Listed as unverified by the CodeKingGTA repo, which asks for before and after wallet footage, replay steps and a save and reload.

Summary: A rumor that stash bags can be sold to a fence more than once. No steps or footage have been published.
Caveats: Listed as unverified by the CodeKingGTA repo, which asks for inventory, buyer, repeated transaction and retained money on video.

Summary: Money glitch videos dated before November 19, 2026 cannot show real gameplay because nobody outside Rockstar had the game.
Caveats: Example: GlitchMod lists a story-mode unlimited money video credited to KuDuRoO and dated September 1, 2026, with no method and an "Unverified" label. Leonida Explorer says every pre-launch money glitch was speculation or a scam funnel.

Glitch: "A car and a browser" infinite money thread
Summary: A viral thread on X that reads like glitch steps but is a joke advertisement for an online casino.
Caveats: The steps end at a real-money gambling site. Nothing in the thread affects in-game money.

Summary: Websites and downloads that promise to add GTA VI money to your account.
Caveats: GTA VI money lives in a local single-player save, so an outside site cannot add to it. The CodeKingGTA repo flags these as an account and malware risk. Never enter credentials or run unknown installers.

Summary: A November 19 video claims a repeatable cocaine-selling loop paying about $15,000 the first time and $3,000 to $4,000 on each later visit. IGN also mentions a variant where players fence the goods first, then save and reload to refill the location.
Payout: Claimed, not demonstrated: about $15,000 first, then $3,000 to $4,000 per visit.
Tips: Wait for an uncut clip showing the balance before and after, a save and reload, and the build number.
Caveats: The CodeKingGTA v2 repo lists it as "Community claim; not validated" and has not confirmed that it differs from a normal restocking activity. It is not clear whether the video and the variant IGN mentions are the same method. It may simply be the warehouse respawn (M-01) at another location.
